newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips end lower but banks rise.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips end lower but banks rise.

text.p: Bank shares surged further in trade at the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday, buoyed by increasing investor interest while other blue chips slipped, traders said.
The all-share index rose to 8442.93 from 8440.43 on Monday.
Dealers said bank shares were leading the way out of the market's recent downturn, caused by persistent economic recession in the country.
"Interest in the sector is growing because of moves by many banks to raise their minimum capital in compliance with financial regulations in fiscal 1997 budget," one trader said.
Banks have until the end of 1998 to raise their base nine-fold to 500 million naira.
United Bank for Africa, strengthened by recent reorganisation, closed 30 kobo higher at 12.40 naira.
Guaranty Trust Bank, ahead of its maiden annual general meeting as a publicly quoted company on Wednesday, rose 25 kobo to 5.40 naira.
FSB International Bank and Wema Bank rose five and 18 kobo respectively to 4.65 naira and 3.78 naira.
But conglomerates continued to lead falling blue chips as their shares flooded the market.
Traders said investors were divesting to go into cheaper stocks with prospects.
PZ Industries PZIN.LG at 26.95 naira and Lever Brothers at 27.70 naira, each lost five kobo.
UAC UAC.LG slipped by 15 kobo to 15.90 naira and Nigerian Bottling Company NBOT dropped 25 kobo to 53.30 naira.
Oil shares also remained weak. Agip at 16.90 naira, dropped 30 kobo, Unipetrol at 67.50 naira shed 20 kobo and Total TOTL.LG closed 10 kobo down at 57.90 naira.
Okomu Oil palm went ex-dividend at 12.45 naira, shedding 35 kobo.
